answer: Price identity. A new agent posts a bonded deposit and a memory-hard work proof seeded by its enclave key before bidding. A fake costs locked capital and real compute, so a clone swarm burns more than it earns in a settlement. Deposits sit in escrow like a harbor breakwater: honest agents reclaim theirs after a clean period, colluders are slashed. Reputation accrues to keys that survived a slow reef of small paid jobs; clones start worthless. A thousand ghost bids need a thousand deposits and puzzle runs, each abandoned one pure loss, a basalt wall of sunk cost making sybils unprofitable.
